text: # Every push to main publishes a release when CHANGELOG.md has entries under
# "## Unreleased". The bump is patch, or minor/major when a PR merged since
# the last tag has the label `release:minor` or `release:major`. A merge with
# an empty Unreleased section (docs, CI, refactors) publishes nothing.
# The tip of main, not the pushed sha: a queued run must see the
# release commit an earlier run pushed.
# Ubuntu 24.04 lets no unconfined program make a user namespace, and bwrap needs one.
# Code under cfg(debug_assertions) hides release-only warnings from the
# debug builds; users install the release build.
# Until Phase P of fleetd: many tests do not run on Windows yet. The gate of Phase P removes this line.
# auto-release.yml calls this after it pushes the tag: a tag pushed with
# GITHUB_TOKEN does not trigger the push event above.
# macOS tar would add AppleDouble `._*` entries for extended attributes.
# The task ledger (docs/specs/task-ledger.md). Bundled: no system SQLite.
# Every `unsafe` block states why it is sound in a `// SAFETY:` note.

//! Reducing a Starlight docs page to plain content HTML.
//! The docs site is Astro Starlight with Expressive Code, which wraps content in
//! presentation markup that a generic HTML-to-markdown pass turns into noise:
//! * The page `<h1>` sits in a sibling panel, *outside* `.sl-markdown-content`,
//!   so a naive extraction loses every page title.
//! * Each heading carries an `<a class="sl-anchor-link">` holding an icon and a
//! `Section titled "..."`, which would otherwise
//!   appear as stray link text after every heading.
//! * Code blocks are not `<pre><code>` with a language class. They are
//!   `div.expressive-code > figure.frame > pre[data-language] > code`, where the
//!   code is split into one `div.ec-line` per line and every token is a `<span>`
//!   with inline colours. Converting that directly loses the language, gains a
//!   blank line per token, and picks up the "Terminal window" caption and the
//!   copy-to-clipboard button.
//! So the DOM is walked once and re-serialised into simple HTML that htmd can
//! convert faithfully.

//! `herdr-install` - installs the latest Herdr CLI.
//! The Rust port of <https://herdr.dev/install.sh> and <https://herdr.dev/install.ps1>,
//! as one binary that needs no shell, no curl, and no PowerShell. It reads the same
//! release manifests as `herdr update`, so installs and updates agree on what
//! "latest" means.

//!   * macOS and Linux get one binary at `~/.local/bin/herdr` from the stable
//!     channel.
//!   * Windows gets the preview channel - the only one that publishes a Windows
//!     asset while native Windows support is in beta - unpacked with its ConPTY
//!     runtime into a versioned directory, with `current` and the PATH directory
//!     pointed at it by junction so an update never overwrites a running
//!     `herdr.exe`.

//! The run of 1 reconcile pass.
//! `docs/specs/fleetd/design.md`, "The reconcile pass" (RR-4, RR-7, FM-7,
//! FM-11, FM-12, PL-5). [`Pass::run`] runs 1 pass in 3 parts:
//! 1. It reads the facts with no transaction, each scan within its budget

//!    missing outbox of each live attempt of its outbox scan (Q3 of
//!    `docs/tickets/fleetd-p5/MAP.md`). It reads the last passed
//!    `worktree_list` run of each repository from `jobs`. It runs no git.
//! 2. In 1 transaction it calls these steps, in this order:
//!    `check_generation`, `tick_fleet_clock`, the ingest of the outbox,
//!    wrapper and job result files, the needs-you item of the operator
//!    token, `observe_intents`,
//!    `mark_orphans`, `finish_exited`, `reconcile_worktrees`,
//!    `disk_budget` (it gives the hold of the worktree disk budget from the
//!    rows that the reconciler wrote), the run

//!    the `worktree_list` job of each repository in each period,
//!    `record_hold_changes` and `intended_effects`. The worktree
//!    observations and orphan marks come before the run duties and the job
//!    queues (stops come before launches). Each effect is a row in an
//!    intended state when the transaction commits. No effect occurs inside
//!    it. The run duties have a [`DutyBudget`]: at most `pass_budget` rows
//!    of each paged duty, and no new duty work after the time budget of the
//!    pass.

//!    the time budget of the pass ends. The rest stay intended rows for the
//!    next pass. When time is left, the run duties do their effects. It
//!    archives the job result files that the transaction ingested. Then it
//!    writes the heartbeat and pings the watchdog.

//! Every `check_every_s` each working worker gets 1 `checks` row. The rules,
//! in order:
//! 1. The agent's process is gone: `dead` at once. A process that does not
//!    exist cannot resume.
//! 2. The agent recorded progress since the last check: `progress`.
//! 3. A proxy checkin: the transcript grew, herdr's state counter moved, or
//!    the working timer ran the whole interval (10m, then 20m, 10 min
//!    apart). The watchdog records progress for the agent.
//! 4. Suspect: the timer ran less than the clock (10m, then 15m, 10 min
//!    apart: it stopped about 5 min ago). Verified at once: herdr still
//!    showing `working` goes to rule 5; else `no_progress`.
//! 5. Nothing else moved, but herdr shows `working`: a proxy checkin.
//! 6. Nothing moved: `no_progress`, and 1 more stall round. The first one
//!    asks the worker for an update.
//! No check reaps a worker: "3 checks of 600 s" ended with Phase 2 of
//! fleetd. The leases and the stall ladder of the pass judge each live
//! attempt (`docs/tickets/fleetd-p2/MAP.md`, Q14). `check_every_s` and
//! `stall_rounds` of a run stay stored.
//! A note names the signals the watchdog could not read ("no timer format
//! for harness pi; no transcript"), so `ledger show` explains why a worker
//! shows no progress.
//! This module decides and records the checks. The caller writes the wakes
//! ([`super::wakes`]). Both `horch ledger watch` and the pass of fleetd
//! (`fleetd/fleet_runtime/adapters/watchdog_duties.rs`) use these rules.

//! A run with an open question starts on Phase 5. After the update, it has
//! 1 idea row and 1 feature row, and its question has 1 owner, the
//! sub-orchestrator `idea-lead:<feature id>`. The old orchestrator gets no
//! message, no task is lost, and the run's `MAP.md` stays readable by
//! `horch ledger add-map --dry-run`.
//! The Phase 5 ledger is built by the real migration steps: the project and
//! the run `r1` are written before the step of [`schema::PHASE_4_VERSION`],
//! so its backfill gives the run its feature row, then the ledger goes to
//! [`schema::PHASE_5_VERSION`]. The other rows of the run in flight are
//! written as a Phase 5 binary left them:
//! - the orchestrator of the run, in the pane `w1:p1`;
//! - [`RUNNING_TASK`] `running`, with its live push attempt, its lease and
//!   its task folder;
//! - [`QUEUED_TASK`] `pending`: it waits for [`RUNNING_TASK`];
//! - [`DONE_TASK`] `done`;
//! - 1 open question of [`RUNNING_TASK`]: its mail question, delivered to
//!   the orchestrator before the update, its `questions` row owned by the
//!   orchestrator, and its `question` event;
//! - the `fleetd` row of the Phase 5 fleetd.
//! The orchestrator, the worker of the live attempt and the old fleetd are
//! stand-ins: `sleep` processes that the rows name.
//! The update: the test stops the old fleetd, migrates the ledger to
//! [`schema::PHASE_6_VERSION`] and starts `horch fleetd` of this branch,

## A HOLD ACTION (the income is higher while the player holds a button). The contract has no argument for it in
## `step`. Use this pattern:
##     static func active(state, data, seconds) -> Array:
##         state["hold_credit"] = float(state["hold_credit"]) + seconds     # the hand gives hold time
##         return []
##     static func step(state, data, dt) -> Array:
##         var credit: float = float(state["hold_credit"])
##         var held: float = minf(credit, dt)                               # the part of this step with the hold
##         state["hold_credit"] = credit - held
##         ... income = rate x (dt - held) + rate x hold_factor x held ...
## - The session calls `active(dt)` and then `step(dt)` in each frame while the button is down.
## - The bench calls `step` for `decision_s` and then `active(decision_s x active_share)` 1 time. The credit is
##   thus used in the steps of the next decision: the hold of the bot is 1 decision late, and the share of the
##   time with the hold is `active_share`.
## - `hold_credit` is state. It is in the save file, or the session sets it to 0 after a load.
